governed.reasoning: Speech tier from v22 (operator-approved 2026-10-26): the bot edits the title and body of a pull request it opened. author_scope own: the route holder refuses a pull request whose author is not the calling seat's bot. Label changes keep the operator's label-only row under GH_SHIM_BYPASS=operator; reviewers, assignees, base, milestones and projects are refused before routing.

Speech tier from v22: resolving a pull request review thread changes only that thread's public state, like closing an issue. The shim admits one inline resolveReviewThread mutation whose only input is threadId; the route holder checks the thread belongs to the bound repository.
Speech tier from v22, the inverse of resolveReviewThread, declared together so a resolution is reversible by the same seat.

admin.reasoning: Administration from v22, the same class as pr merge: gh stack merge lands a stack through the asynchronous merge endpoint under the operator's identity, with the audited bypass.

The gh-stack extension calls the GitHub API in-process with gh's own login, never through gh, so this verb would speak as the operator. Refused with the bot route named (git push, gh pr create, gh api on the stacks endpoints); runs only as audited operator administration under GH_SHIM_BYPASS=operator.

gh stack push writes the stack's branches to GitHub with the operator's git credentials, always as a --force-with-lease push (github/gh-stack cmd/push.go:103-109 calling internal/git/gitops.go:258-305), so it is the operator writing, not the bot: refused with the bot route named, or run as audited operator administration under GH_SHIM_BYPASS=operator.

mechanical.reasoning: gh-stack subcommands whose source makes no GitHub write: reads under the operator's login and local git work only.

api_rules.rationale: bot reply in a pull request review thread; body only
routed as pr edit (author_scope own); title and body only, base refused
create a pull request stack as the bot; pull_requests only
append pull requests to a stack as the bot; pull_requests only
dissolve a stack as the bot; no payload
asynchronous merge, the same class as pr merge; operator identity, audited bypass
